source_span: If there was that credibility, market probabilities of a hike with 15 days to go before the meeting would be in the 90s instead of 68%
source_chain: Warsh's hawkish-toned Jackson Hole speech avoided challenging the government/fiscal drivers of inflation, so it added volatility but not credibility, therefore the market's September-hike probability sits at an anomalously low 68% versus the 90-100% typical this close to a meeting, and with the Dallas Fed trimmed mean (2.35% 6M) and core PCE (3.5% 6M) already near Taylor-Rule-implied levels plus softening ISM/JOLTS data, therefore Blitz expects Warsh finds 'wiggle room' to hold rather than hike, with the 9/11 CPI print as the invalidating data point if it runs hot.
pulse_chain: Warsh's hawkish message plus Governor Barr's hike support convinced the market the Fed tightens into a slowdown, therefore hike odds ran 27%->69% and long bond yields are breaking across three countries with vol-control funds maxed and forced-selling risk, and separately 'the hold case is being made by Goldman' citing the Dallas Fed trimmed mean (2.35%), core PCE (3.5%), and Treasury issuance-vs-Fed-holdings growth (6.8% vs 0.7%) even though 'Goldman's own screen shows 66% odds of a hike,' with September 11 CPI (attributed to JPMorgan) as the resolving print.
why: The pulse lifts TS Lombard/Blitz's entire hold-case argument and its exact supporting statistics (Dallas Fed trimmed mean 2.35%, core PCE 3.5% 6M, Treasury stock +6.8% vs Fed holdings +0.7%) and attributes them to Goldman Sachs, a bank that never made this argument in any sourced note, while dropping TS Lombard's actual mechanism — that Warsh's credibility deficit is why the hike probability is anomalously low versus historical precedent, not merely soft inflation data.
